  content = '## Marvel''s Legal Comedy

She-Hulk was Marvel''s boldest experiment — a half-hour legal comedy that broke the fourth wall, commented on its own franchise, and directly addressed the toxic fandom discourse happening in real-time. It wasn''t for everyone, and it knew it. That self-awareness was either its greatest strength or its most divisive quality.

## Daredevil Returns

Charlie Cox''s return as Matt Murdock — now in the classic yellow suit — was the show''s most universally praised element. His chemistry with Tatiana Maslany crackled, and the episode proved that Daredevil could work in a lighter tone while maintaining his charm. It set up anticipation for Born Again perfectly.

## Breaking the Fourth Wall (and K.E.V.I.N.)

The finale''s meta-commentary — with She-Hulk literally breaking out of Disney+ to confront K.E.V.I.N., an AI version of Kevin Feige — was either genius or too clever by half. It acknowledged every criticism of the show and the MCU formula, then chose to do something different anyway.

## Fun Facts

- The show''s VFX became a major discussion point about Marvel''s treatment of VFX artists
- Tatiana Maslany won an Emmy for Orphan Black, playing multiple characters
- The twerking scene with Megan Thee Stallion became one of the most discussed MCU moments
- Charlie Cox filmed his episodes during a break from Daredevil: Born Again production
- The show directly referenced and mocked online hate campaigns against it',
